rejected.trait: Keeping the shim and fixing the price line by hand
rejected.reason: The shim accepted a bare ReactNode in a slot, so it checked neither leaf identity nor declared props - the price-line mismatch was the FIRST such defect, not the only possible one, and patching it would have left the rest to surface one file at a time. Removing the shim turns every remaining mismatch into a compile error in one pass.

rejected.reason: price-discount-line is LOCKED and already says what a price line looks like. A course page that redefines the shared price line is how two pages stop showing prices the same way. The visual moves to what the locked entry declares.

rejected.trait: Applying with the three ports undeclared
rejected.reason: verify_apply_materialization compares landed bytes to the sealed hash and reports an undeclared difference as a substitution, because it cannot tell an alias rewrite from a component swapped for a similar one. Blocking there and declaring afterwards would be a permission written by the party it excuses.

rejected.reason: It cannot compile. ContractKey is closed over the entries on disk, so the locked Tree refuses a proposed key until the merge lands - which is the whole reason the candidate carries a shim.

revisionHistory.summary: One repair and one settled question, both raised by the Apply lock's redetection before any production file was written. Neither changes a pixel: the candidate adopts production's own CoverImage, and the [locale] route segment is confirmed as intended rather than assumed.
retained: Every rendered state is byte-identical to 1.1 except CoverImage's comment text; the design was not touched.

rejected.trait: Materializing the sealed CoverImage over production's
rejected.reason: The courses-catalog run had already landed this leaf, and production's copy is the NEWER one: it records that naming the ESLint directive in a comment trips the gate, because the rule matches the token in source text and prose about a suppression reads to it exactly like a suppression. The seal carried the older wording. Writing it would have undone another approved run's repair under a seal that says it was reviewed - so the candidate adopts production's file instead, making materialization a verified no-op.

rejected.trait: Dropping the [locale] segment to match the repository's flat routes
rejected.reason: Apply raised it as drift because no other route in this repository carries [locale]; the user answered that the segment is intended, so the production URL /vi/courses/fullstack-mastery is reproduced. The alternative offered - moving api, authentication, courses, dashboard, league and profile under [locale] - was declined as a whole-repository migration that belongs to its own Plan run, not to this Apply.

rejected.trait: Silently writing the route to whichever path existed
rejected.reason: Either direction would have been an undeclared target, which is the substitution the seal exists to prevent. The question was settled here, in Preview, where a path is still reviewable.

Keeping it means the materialization verifier compares production against an approved hash and confirms they match. Removing it would leave the leaf unchecked at exactly the moment it was found to be the risky one.

unknowns: Whether the production course query returns pricing phases in ladder order or requires client sorting. The candidate renders the fixture's order as given.
Whether a course can publish zero value propositions. The candidate renders the promise section unconditionally; if the empty case exists it is a Fidelity Fix, not a redesign.

decisions: The page frame carries no horizontal inset and no bottom padding so the pinned bar reaches both edges and rests flush. The measure moves to course-breadcrumb-row and main-then-rail, and main-then-rail closes the page's bottom space.
CurriculumModuleRow is a leaf, not a contract. ContractHost does not admit `details` and should not: a disclosure is an intrinsic control with its own open state, not a shape that holds other shapes.
A module with no lessons renders flat rather than as a disclosure. An empty disclosure invites a press that opens onto nothing, which reads as broken rather than empty.
not-found offers no recovery action and failed does. There is no retry that could change a not-found answer, and an action that cannot help is worse than none.
The pinned bar shows the rail's resolved price string rather than deriving its own, so the two can never disagree - including while pending, when both rest.
Resting run lengths are read from each entry's restingCount rather than written in the page, so a skeleton cannot keep claiming five modules after the entry settles on three.

Tree emits role="list" for ul and ol hosts. Tailwind preflight sets list-style: none, and Safari answers that by dropping the element from the accessibility tree - so the list the entry just claimed is announced as loose text.

integrationEdits.reason: Emit role="list" when the entry's host is ul or ol. Tailwind preflight sets list-style: none on every list and Safari answers by dropping the element from the accessibility tree, so the list the entry claims is announced as loose text. The candidate proves this in its own Tree shim; the locked frame needs the same three lines.
The candidate file is MERGED into the locked registry, not written over it: 17 entries are added and LayoutClassName gains twelve members. Everything already in the locked file stays.

The route does not exist in the target. Apply creates it together with the single-course GraphQL document and its SWR hook; the candidate has no request pipeline and drives its states from a fixture. The folder carries NO locale segment because the locale is not in the folder: src/middleware.ts runs next-intl's middleware over every non-api, non-asset path and prefixes it, so this file is served at /vi/courses/<displayId> - the production baseline URL - with src/app staying flat exactly as every other route in this repository does.
The connected half does not exist in the candidate. The candidate page takes one settled situation, while production settles the rail and the curriculum independently.
The candidate reads resolved Vietnamese strings from its fixture. Apply moves them into the catalogue under a courses.detail namespace and the connected half resolves them through useTranslations.

The rail's action label is a resolved string passed in by the connected half; the presentational rail has no enrolment concept and cannot differ by persona. Whether an enrolled viewer sees a different label is a connected-half decision Apply makes against the backend, not a tree this candidate can render.
The candidate pins locale vi and imports the target's real vi catalogue; it has no request pipeline to resolve a second locale. Recorded as a difference rather than claimed as coverage.

contracts.why: Reused verbatim. The only entry in the repository that declares a host today; every rendered state opens exactly one.
Reused verbatim by both the rail and the pinned bar, so the two can never disagree about what the course costs.
Carries no horizontal inset and no bottom padding, so the pinned bar reaches both edges of a phone and rests flush on its bottom edge.
The trail back is a set of destinations rather than prose, so it is a nav a reader can jump to.

Mirrors the locked rail-then-main on the opposite child. A left rail and a right rail are the same mechanics and neither should be expressed by reordering content. It also closes the page's bottom space, which the frame cannot do without lifting the pinned bar off its edge.
What the course is, promises and contains is one continuous argument addressed to one reader.
The course name and the sentence qualifying it are read as a unit before any evidence or price.
Unordered peer facts that wrap together. Deliberately not profile-topic-chip-run: identical mechanics, different domain.
Exists only to be the list item. Added after the exported HTML showed the ul holding spans - the run had been claiming a length nothing could count.
A named region is its heading and the body that heading introduces; the name travels with the content to anything navigating by region.
Promises are unordered peers of one joined list. Deliberately not profile-evidence-list, whose identical mechanics are named for a different domain.
The affirmative mark leads the sentence it affirms, and the sentence owns the remaining width so it wraps under itself rather than under the mark.
Modules are ORDERED: module three follows module two and cannot be read first, so an ol says the sequence to a reader who cannot see the numbering.
A details element cannot be an ol's child and leave the sequence intact. Separating them also puts the list's padding on the item, so an open module's lessons stay inside the same inset as its title.
The buy box is complementary to the narrative rather than part of it, which is what an aside means and what assistive technology announces.
The payable price, what it saves and what is running out are one claim about cost, so they sit tighter to each other than to the ladder below.
The open phase is the price and the ones after it are the cost of waiting, so the sequence IS the meaning.
One phase states its availability and its price on a single baseline. The mark keeps a fixed slot whether or not this phase is open, which is what keeps the names aligned.

Deliberately NO host. The rail already claims the complementary region for this page's commerce; announcing a second one on the single viewport where only the pinned copy is reachable would be worse than announcing none.

vocabularyProposals.why: Measured with a bracket-aware scan: the entries use 51 distinct classes and twelve are not in the 117-member union. Every one mirrors a member already present for the opposite child or the opposite edge - the union holds all five sticky members for first-child, and holds top-0, border-b, hidden and py-6. Nothing in this repository has had a right-hand rail or a bottom-pinned bar before, which is why nobody noticed.

A native details disclosure. It is a leaf and not a contract because ContractHost does not admit `details` and should not: a disclosure is an intrinsic control with its own open state. HeroUI 3.2.4 ships no Accordion, Collapsible or Disclosure and the repository has no accordion branch - both checked.
Carried over unchanged from the superseded run and shared with the catalog run. Same proposal, same target path.
CoursePricingRail and CourseMobileEnrollBar are the first blocks in a courses domain; the existing folders are auth, dashboard and profile.

approval.restatement: Thầy duyệt revision 1.0 như đang hiển thị chứ? Có "duyệt" thì em mới viết và niêm design-record.json. - answered "duyêht". Revision 1.1 then repaired one parity divergence found in the 375px screenshot, and the instruction to carry that through to the seal was "Lam tiep cai nay di, sao mai van khong approve dc". Revision 1.2 then adopted production's own CoverImage and settled the [locale] route segment - both raised by the Apply lock before any production file was written. The instruction covering it was "ok" to a stated plan of "1.2 then Apply", and the routing answer was the explicit choice "Chi route course detail" from a question that also offered a whole-repository migration and a flat path. Revision 1.3 is record-only, made inside the same "1.2 then Apply" authorisation and against the same confirmed write boundary: it declares three ported files whose bytes cannot match the seal, and changes no candidate source. Revision 1.4 was authorised by "ok" to a stated plan that named its purpose exactly - drop the shim so every remaining mismatch becomes a compile error in one pass - and its visual consequences are listed in revisionHistory[0].visualChanges rather than left to be noticed. Revision 1.5 is record-only and CORRECTS an error of mine: the [locale] question was put to the user on a wrong reading of the repository, and the answer they gave - add the segment - is already what the repository does, in middleware rather than in folders.
approval.source: duyêht / Lam tiep cai nay di, sao mai van khong approve dc / ok (1.2 then Apply) / Chi route course detail / (1.3 record-only, same authorisation) / ok (1.4, drop the shim) / (1.5 record-only correction)
approval.note: Recorded as two utterances rather than one because they approve two different things: the first names revision 1.0 after it was restated back, the second instructs the seal to proceed after 1.1 was reported. Neither is presented as approval of the other, and the second is an instruction to continue rather than a fresh naming of 1.1 - which is exactly why the restatement above keeps both in full instead of paraphrasing them into one clean approval.
